summary: Andrew Getty, one of the heirs to billions of oil money, appears to have died of natural causes, a Los Angeles Police Department spokesman said. Andrew Getty, 47, had "several health issues," Aguilar said, adding that an autopsy will be conducted.

Jennifer Stewart's 2-year-old cat Felix remained missing nearly a week after arriving at JFK on an April 1 Etihad Airways flight from Abu Dhabi; Stewart believes he escaped because his carrier was crushed. Etihad is investigating and searching with airport ground handlers and hired specialists, and says it will review its pet-handling procedures.

Shanghai, like many large Chinese cities, rations license plates as it looks for a solution to its gridlocked roads and polluted skies. Each month there are around 10,000 license plates available, and Li Lifei, who has been trying for six months with no success, said the final price at the most recent auction was 80,600 yuan ($13,000). Another option would be to buy a hybrid vehicle that automatically qualifies for a license plate, but Chinese drivers haven't wholeheartedly embraced the concept and few Chinese have American-style garages where the vehicles can be charged overnight. For others, the hassles of buying and owning a car have become too much: a recent report by consultants Bain & Company found that, of 2,137 people it surveyed, some 40% said cars were losing their appeal as a status symbol.

Only a few kilometers away, 147 people -- mostly students -- were brutally massacred when Al-Shabaab militants invaded the campus in Garissa, a town in northeastern Kenya. We've come to this particular Islamic religious school because the man suspected by Kenyan authorities of being the "mastermind" behind the atrocity -- Mohamed Mohamud -- once taught here. What worries authorities here is exactly that -- Mohamud was Kenyan. The Kenyan government is concerned that Al-Shabaab is recruiting disaffected youth from inside the country.

Patrick Dempsey's character, Dr. Derek Shepherd, died in Thursday night's episode of "Grey's Anatomy" after a car crash that followed his assistance to victims of another accident. In a statement reported by The Hollywood Reporter, creator Shonda Rhimes described Derek as deeply important to Meredith Grey, herself and viewers, and said his absence would be widely felt. Dempsey's departure came with a year still remaining on his contract. Fans reacted with grief and feelings of betrayal, People magazine published a character obituary, and #McDreamyForever trended on Twitter. The series will continue, with its 11th season ending in May and Ellen Pompeo, who plays Derek's wife Meredith, contracted through season 12. Rhimes had identified Meredith's independence as the season's theme, and Derek's death makes that challenge more immediate. In the week ending April 19, the show ranked 20th for total viewers and 12th among adults aged 18–49. Dempsey told TVLine he was grateful for the experience and the fans' dedication. He also has a development agreement with ABC Studios, which produces the series.

Ebony Dickens of East Point, Georgia, posted her Facebook rant under the name Tiffany Milan, police said. East Point police Lt. Cliff Chandler told WSB that she was talking about killing 15 people within a day or so, saying, "whether she is serious or not that's something that we have to take seriously." East Point police said the posts threatened white officers specifically and "indicated that the acts were being plotted and were in motion." The East Point police, Atlanta police, FBI and federal Homeland Security Department were involved. The post was removed a day later, just before Dickens was arrested, CNN affiliate WSB reported. After connecting Dickens to the Facebook post, authorities obtained a search warrant for her residence and took her into custody while executing that warrant. "A firearm along with three computers was located during the search," East Point police said. Dickens, 33, appeared in court Wednesday on a charge of disseminating information related to terrorist acts. A judge set a $10,000 bond for her and banned her from social media. She was then transferred to Fulton County Jail, where she remained until bonding out at 6:19 a.m. Thursday, according to county sheriff's office spokeswoman Tracy Flanagan.
